name: Dumbbell Bench Press
grip: Pronated to slightly semi-neutral (angled approx. 45 degrees).
description: Lie supine on a flat bench and press two dumbbells vertically from chest level to full arm extension, controlling the descent to a comfortable stretch.
setup: Sit on the edge of a flat horizontal bench with a dumbbell resting upright on each knee.
Lie back smoothly while guiding the dumbbells to the sides of the lower chest with forearms vertical.
Plant feet firmly flat on the floor, retract shoulder blades, and brace the core.
instructions: Press both dumbbells upward vertically until the arms are fully extended over the mid-chest without locking the elbows.
Keep wrists stacked directly over elbows throughout the press.
Pause under control at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back toward the chest.
Stop when a gentle stretch is felt across the chest, maintaining shoulder blade contact with the bench.
cues: Drive straight up over the chest.
Keep feet planted and shoulder blades pinched.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows straight out to 90 degrees, increasing shoulder stress.
Arching the lower back excessively or lifting hips off the bench.
Clanging the dumbbells together at the top of the repetition.

logging.example: Two 32 kg dumbbells: record 32 kg per dumbbell.
logging.note: Record the mass of an individual dumbbell rather than the combined total weight of both dumbbells.

variantNote: Flat horizontal bench variation. Allows independent arm movement and natural wrist rotation compared to a straight barbell.
